what_this_is: The three SMMUv3 instances the vendor firmware's IORT declares, as the guest sees them. This is what a QEMU model has to match: base, size, and the four interrupt IDs per instance. It does not claim anything about stream-ID mappings, because the IORT carries none for PCI.

source.table: ACPI IORT, 3904 bytes, dumped by the harness from a boot of vendor UEFI 2.158.15 under this profile
source.run: firmware/runs/20261109T065836.074857Z (acpi-IORT-0x87fe8018.bin; the dump is ignored, not committed)
source.how: iasl -d on the dumped IORT; the SMMUv3 nodes are type 04 and the ITS group is type 01
source.why_it_matters: the guest binds arm-smmu-v3 against these addresses and claims them in /proc/iomem, while the profile backs them with an inert window (-10 priority), so to the guest a real SMMU exists and does nothing

interrupt_numbers: These are ACPI GSIVs, which equal the GIC INTID for SPIs. The IORT gives them as 0x156/0x15B/0x155/0x154 for the first instance, 0x16E/0x173/0x16D/0x16C for the second and 0x18D/none/0x18C/0x18B for the third; the values above are decimal.

qemu_model.type: arm-smmuv3 (TYPE_ARM_SMMUV3), a sysbus device with one 0x20000 mmio region and four irqs
qemu_model.irq_order: index 0 = event, 1 = PRI, 2 = cmdq sync, 3 = gerror (include/hw/arm/smmuv3.h: SMMU_IRQ_EVTQ, SMMU_IRQ_PRIQ, SMMU_IRQ_CMD_SYNC, SMMU_IRQ_GERROR)
qemu_model.creation_pattern: hw/arm/virt.c's create_smmu(): qdev_new, set primary-bus, memory and secure-memory links, sysbus_realize_and_unref, sysbus_mmio_map(0, base), then sysbus_connect_irq per line
qemu_model.mapping_note: the profile's inert SoC block is added with priority -10, so a device mapped at priority 0 over the same range wins without carving the block apart
qemu_model.third_instance: its PRI line is 0 in the IORT, so the model should leave that irq unconnected rather than inventing an interrupt

cannot_be_modelled_as_declared.measured: two attempts have named QEMU refusals in this record: with no primary-bus QEMU refuses at realize ("SMMU is not attached to any PCI bus!"), and with primary-bus on all three it refuses the second ("An iommu is already attached to this bus"). The original startup logs are not associated with a retained run here; the earlier count of three measured attempts is unsupported by the retained diagnostics.
cannot_be_modelled_as_declared.source_review: hw/pci/pci.c:3321 rejects a second per-bus IOMMU and hw/arm/smmu-common.c:951 requires PCI attachment. These source guards confirm the limitation structurally; they are not a third measured startup failure.
cannot_be_modelled_as_declared.consequence: QEMU's arm-smmuv3 cannot represent three instances that the firmware declares with no PCI attachment. Attaching one would claim a translation the IORT does not describe, and would route the NIC's DMA through an IOMMU with no stream IDs — the opposite of a faithful model
cannot_be_modelled_as_declared.verdict: the faithful model is the one already in place: the three windows stay inert, the guest claims them and the driver binds to nothing real, and the record says so rather than pretending a model exists
cannot_be_modelled_as_declared.would_change_it: an SMMU model that does not require a PCI bus (QEMU has none), or a platform description that maps a device to one of these instances

not_established: whether modelling these three instances changes the NVMe probe's -EPROBE_DEFER (measured: the deferred device carries no supplier link, so the SMMU is not its dependency)
what stream IDs each instance owns — the IORT has no ID mappings for PCI, so a faithful model cannot yet say which device goes through which SMMU
whether the guest would attach PCI devices to them (no ID mappings and no root-complex node means the answer is probably no, which is why modelling them is safe rather than transformative)

how_to_make_the_change.warning: do not hand-edit hunks in qemu/patches/0001-spark-fw-address-profile.patch: a single blank context line that loses its leading space, or an added block spliced into an existing hunk, makes git apply reject the file while patch(1) still accepts it — the builder uses git apply, so the failure surfaces as 'corrupt patch' at build time
how_to_make_the_change.method: apply the patch by building once, edit build/qemu-src/hw/arm/virt.c, then regenerate the whole patch as a diff against the pristine tree and re-apply it from scratch to confirm git apply --check passes before committing
how_to_make_the_change.verified_by: git apply --check in a throwaway git clone of the pristine v11.1.2 tree
